items.title: SafePal breach exposes 40,000 customers as hardware wallet failures pile up
points: SafePal said a flaw in its order-tracking plugin let attackers access names, emails, and shipping addresses of roughly 40,000 customers, though wallet credentials (the secret keys that control the crypto) were not compromised.
Leaked names and addresses raise the risk of phishing (fake messages tricking users into handing over keys) and physical home invasions targeting known crypto holders.
Coldcard exploit losses are estimated to exceed $150 million, and Trezor's third-party shipping partner separately leaked customer data.
Three incidents across three hardware wallet brands (offline devices meant to store crypto keys securely) point to systemic weakness in vendor and supply-chain security rather than isolated bugs.

items.title: French tax records of 678,000+ taxpayers up for sale
points: A hacker is selling personal and financial records from a June breach affecting more than 678,000 French taxpayers and businesses.
Tax filings can reveal who holds cryptocurrency and roughly how much wealth they have, giving attackers a targeting list.
Shows how non-crypto third-party leaks create secondary attack vectors against coin holders.

items.title: Trump-linked World Liberty stablecoin clears bank charter hurdle
points: The OCC (Office of the Comptroller of the Currency, the U.S. regulator that oversees national banks) granted conditional approval to World Liberty Trust Company.
The entity, tied to Trump's World Liberty Financial, obtained a national trust bank charter, moving it closer to launching a USD-backed stablecoin (a token pegged 1:1 to the dollar).
Marks a notable regulatory milestone for politically connected crypto infrastructure.

items.title: Market check
points: Bitcoin held around $63,850 as traders digested the wave of wallet-maker and infrastructure breaches.

items.title: Jane Street discloses nearly $1B in spot Bitcoin ETFs
points: The Wall Street trading firm reported holding over $990 million in spot Bitcoin ETFs (exchange-traded funds that track Bitcoin's price so buyers get exposure without holding the coin themselves).
The position signals continued institutional appetite for regulated Bitcoin exposure.

sections.title: SafePal Data Breach and Cascading Hardware Wallet Failures
points: SafePal disclosed an order-tracking plugin flaw gave attackers access to names, emails, and shipping addresses of approximately 40,000 customers
Exposed personal data creates vulnerability to phishing attacks and physical home invasions targeting wallet holders, even though wallet credentials remained secure

Pattern of breaches expanding: Coldcard exploit losses estimated at $150 million, Trezor's third-party shipping partner exposed customer data, SafePal's separate vulnerability suggests systematic security weaknesses across the hardware wallet industry
Risk extends beyond direct victims—leaked customer lists enable attackers to target specific high-value individuals known to hold significant cryptocurrency

sections.title: French Tax Records Leak Threatens Crypto Holders Globally
points: Hacker selling personal and financial records from June data breach affecting 678,000+ French taxpayers and businesses

Breach demonstrates how third-party data leaks outside the crypto ecosystem can expose cryptocurrency holders' identities and create secondary attack vectors
